bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Museum ranked in top 10, Becomes Asia's highest-ranked museum ahead of New York's Metropolitan Museum Of Art; check top 10 Patna's Bihar Museum has secured the ninth position in the list of the world's 100 best museums for 2026, earning recognition as the highest-ranked museum in Asia. The ranking was released by German travel guide and digital magazine Worth a Journey. The Bihar Museum has secured a place ahead of some of the world's most renowned institutions, including the Musée du Louvre in Paris and the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York. The achievement has brought international recognition to Bihar's cultural and historical heritage, placing the state on the global museum map. Bihar Museum Ranks Ninth Among World's Best Museums According to the 2026 rankings, the Bihar Museum is the only Asian museum to feature in the global top 10. It has been placed ninth, ahead of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, which secured the tenth position. The top five museums on the list include Mexico City's Museo Nacional de Antropología, Madrid's Museo del Prado, Louisiana Museum of Modern Art in Denmark, Saint Petersburg's State Hermitage Museum in Russia and Vienna's Kunsthistorisches Museum in Austria. Other museums featured in the top 10 include Türkiye's Şanlıurfa Archaeology Museum, Poland's Museum of the Second World War and the National WWII Museum in the United States. Live Events What Makes Bihar Museum Special? Located on Bailey Road in Patna, the Bihar Museum is known for its extensive collection of historical and cultural artefacts. The museum houses a wide range of exhibits, including ancient sculptures, coins, manuscripts, historical objects and traditional folk art. It offers visitors an opportunity to explore Bihar's rich history, cultural traditions and artistic heritage. Its collections highlight different periods of the region's past and showcase its contribution to India's cultural legacy. Bihar Museum's Global Recognition The museum's ninth-place ranking in the 2026 global list marks an important milestone for Bihar's cultural institutions. Its position as the highest-ranked museum in Asia also brings attention to India's historical collections and heritage. Top 10 Museums in the World 2026 1. Museo Nacional de Antropología – Mexico 2. bihar_raw_news.title: Why Bihar Museum is in the spotlight: The Didarganj Yakshi and the Worth a Journey ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Why Bihar Museum is in the spotlight: The Didarganj Yakshi and the Worth a Journey ranking behind the buzz Bihar Museum ranks ninth on Worth a Journey’s 2026 museum list. Explore its courtyard architecture, Didarganj Yakshi, history galleries and the Cosmic Garden exhibition now on view in Patna. Business Today Desk Updated Oct 31, 2026, 8:31 AM IST 1 / 6 Bihar Museum is number nine on Worth a Journey’s The World’s 100 Best Museums 2026 list. The travel guide also names it the highest-ranked museum in Asia on that list. The Patna museum’s entry highlights its history collections, sculpture galleries and children’s section. 2 / 6 Maki and Associates designed the museum as a campus of connected buildings, working with Mumbai-based Opolis. Courtyards and corridors link its different sections. Weathering-steel surfaces give the exterior its distinctive rust-like colour, alongside finishes in local stone, terracotta and glass. 3 / 6 One of the museum’s signature objects is the Didarganj Yakshi, a Chunar sandstone figure holding a fly-whisk. The museum records its discovery at Didarganj, Patna, in 1917. Standing 5 feet 2 inches tall, it is known for its polished surface and carefully carved details. 4 / 6 The galleries move through Bihar’s history, with sections covering the Mauryas, Sungas, Kushanas, Guptas and Palas. Elsewhere, visitors find Patna School paintings and regional art. A visible-storage section follows the development of coins and displays terracotta objects and sculptures. 5 / 6 An interactive Grand Trunk Road map, sculpture puzzles and fossil replicas give young visitors ways to explore history and natural science. The museum’s Children’s Gallery also uses dramatic re-creations and storytelling, with sections covering Chandragupta Maurya and Sher Shah Suri. 6 / 6 On view from October 22 to November 15, 2026, Cosmic Garden pairs paintings and sculptures by Madhvi Parekh and Manu Parekh with hand-embroidered works by Karishma Swali and the Chanakya School of Craft. The exhibition previously appeared at the 2024 Venice Biennale as a collateral event. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Asks District Education Officers to Drive AI Adoption Across Government Schools and ...
bihar_raw_news.content: News School Education Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Copy URL Bihar’s Education Department has asked district education officers (DEOs) across the state to actively encourage officials and staff in government schools and educational institutions to use artificial intelligence tools in their day-to-day academic and administrative work. Generative AI applications such as ChatGPT and Claude are named in the advisory as examples. According to reports in Hindustan , the letter went out to all DEOs on Friday, 30 October 2026, on the direction of Additional Chief Secretary (Education) C K Anil, who took charge of the department only a day earlier. Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari had separately asked the department to prepare a detailed action plan for bringing AI into its functioning. From drafting letters to monitoring schemes The advisory frames AI primarily as a productivity aid for the education bureaucracy rather than a classroom tool. It notes that AI adoption in education is accelerating globally and argues that such tools can save time, simplify routine work and improve efficiency. Specific use cases flagged include drafting official letters and circulars, as well as supporting the monitoring and review of departmental schemes and programmes at the district level. DEOs have been asked to build awareness among their teams and motivate officers and employees to try these applications. State-wide licences and iGOT-based training The education push sits within a broader state government effort. As reported, a communication from Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit states that the Department of Information Technology is in the process of procuring licences for OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Google Gemini and Microsoft Copilot, with each department set to receive one licence of each tool. A list of free AI tools for general use, spanning categories such as chatbots, writing, image and video creation, presentations and voice, has also been circulated, and staff are free to use other applications as well. For capacity building, departments have been asked to draw on iGOT, the Government of India’s online learning platform for civil servants. The IT Department is also preparing an AI training framework covering all officers as well as regular and contractual staff, and departments have been asked to identify participants and their training needs. Each department has further been requested to designate a Joint Secretary-level officer and an IT manager as nodal officers for the initiative. Why it matters The move is notable for where it places AI first: in the administrative layer that runs schools, rather than in classrooms. If officials can use these tools to draft routine communication faster and track district-level programmes more closely, the time saved could be redirected to supervision and support for schools, provided adoption is backed by structured training rather than left to individual initiative. The advisory also leaves several questions open, including guidelines on data privacy when official information is entered into commercial AI platforms, checks on the accuracy of AI-drafted communication, and whether the limited number of paid licences will reach district and block offices. bihar_raw_news.title: HPCL Plans to Set Up Rs 159 Crore CBG Plant in Bihar's Bhagalpur - Indian PSU
bihar_raw_news.content: Read in your preferred Language : Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited (HPCL) is set to establish a Rs 159 crore compressed biogas (CBG) plant at Kankaithi in Bhagalpur, Bihar, to convert municipal wet waste into green fuel and organic manure. The proposed project will process 135 tonnes of segregated organic waste daily, offering a waste-management solution alongside renewable energy production. The memorandum of understanding (MoU) between HPCL and Bhagalpur Municipal Corporation is nearing finalisation. A high-level team from the civic body is expected to visit Patna to complete the agreement process. The project is part of Bihar’s efforts to strengthen urban waste management and promote the conversion of organic waste into renewable energy. Plant to Process 135 Tonnes of Wet Waste Daily The proposed facility at the Kankaithi dumping ground will have the capacity to process 135 tonnes of segregated organic waste per day. Wet waste collected from households, hotels, vegetable markets and fruit markets will be processed to produce compressed biogas and organic manure. The biogas can serve as an alternative to conventional compressed natural gas (CNG) in vehicles and other suitable applications. Organic manure produced during the process can also be used in agriculture. HPCL to Invest in Construction and Operations Under the proposed arrangement, Bhagalpur Municipal Corporation will provide 10 acres of land at the Kankaithi dumping ground complex to HPCL free of charge for 25 years. The land will remain under the ownership of the municipal corporation. HPCL will bear the capital expenditure for constructing the plant and installing the necessary machinery, as well as the operational expenditure during the agreed period. At the end of the 25-year agreement, the fully operational facility will be handed over to Bhagalpur Municipal Corporation without additional cost. Civic Body to Provide Supporting Infrastructure Bhagalpur Municipal Corporation will arrange essential infrastructure for the project, including an approach road, electricity connection, water supply, sewerage facilities and surface water drainage. The Bihar Urban Infrastructure Development Corporation (BUIDCO) is expected to coordinate the technical assessment and cost estimation of the required infrastructure. The availability of these facilities will be crucial for the construction and smooth operation of the plant. Boost to Bihar’s Waste-to-Energy Initiatives The proposed Bhagalpur facility is expected to help reduce the volume of organic waste accumulating at dumping grounds while generating commercially useful renewable fuel. The project will combine municipal waste processing with clean energy production, potentially improving the efficiency of the city’s solid waste management system. For Bhagalpur Municipal Corporation, the arrangement offers an opportunity to develop a major waste-processing facility without bearing the primary construction and operating costs. The finalisation of the MoU and completion of the necessary preparatory work will determine the next steps towards implementation. Once operational, the plant is expected to strengthen Bhagalpur’s waste-processing capacity and contribute to Bihar’s broader efforts to promote compressed biogas and sustainable urban waste management. national_raw_news.title: Centre constitutes high-level committee to recommend banking reforms for Viksit Bharat 2047
national_raw_news.content: The government has constituted a High-Level Committee on Banking for Viksit Bharat to review the country’s banking sector and recommend reforms in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The Finance Ministry said that the Committee will recommend structural, institutional, regulatory and legislative reforms to make the Indian banking sector globally competitive, financially inclusive and resilient. The Committee will be chaired by former Central Vigilance Commissioner Suresh N. Patel. Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu, former Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Indian Bank Padmaja Chunduru, and former RBI Deputy Governor N. S. Vishwanathan will be its members. The Joint Secretary (Banking) in the Department of Financial Services will serve as the Member Secretary. The Committee will have a tenure of six months. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman had announced the setting up of the Committee in her Budget speech this year. The Committee will assess existing banking practices and prudential norms, identify global best practices and examine their suitability for adoption in the Indian banking system. It will also review the existing regulatory and legal frameworks governing banks, including Regional Rural Banks and Cooperative Banks, and suggest reforms to improve efficiency and ease of banking. In addition, the Committee will prepare a roadmap for the adoption of artificial intelligence and digital innovations in banking institutions, while recommending safeguards against cyber risks.

national_raw_news.title: EAM calls for prioritising diplomacy over military solutions to resolve global conflicts at G20 m...
national_raw_news.content: India has asserted that military solutions cannot resolve global challenges and that diplomacy must be given an opportunity to address conflicts. Speaking at the first plenary session of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, the United States, last night, External Affairs Minister Dr S. Jaishankar stressed the need to preserve freedom of navigation and ensure an end to attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers, in accordance with international law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). His remarks come amid ongoing conflicts in different parts of the world, including the Russia-Ukraine war and escalating tensions in West Asia. Dr Jaishankar said that countries of the Global South are disproportionately bearing the consequences of attacks on civilian shipping and seafarers. He noted that such attacks are threatening the availability of essential commodities, including fuel, food and fertilisers, and driving up their costs. At least 22 Indians, including 14 seafarers, have lost their lives in West Asia since the conflict began in February this year. The External Affairs Minister, who reached Atlanta on Thursday, also held interactions with his counterparts from several countries ahead of the meeting. Dr Jaishankar will also participate in a QUAD Foreign Ministers’ Meeting with his counterparts from Japan, Australia and the United States on the sidelines of the G20 meeting. The United States is scheduled to host the G20 Leaders’ Summit in Miami on 14 and 15 December. Following his engagements in Atlanta, Dr Jaishankar is scheduled to travel to St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda, to lead India’s delegation to the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting, scheduled from 1 to 4 November.

national_raw_news.title: ISRO launches NVS-03 satellite to strengthen indigenous navigation capabilities; Vice President a...
national_raw_news.content: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has successfully launched its next-generation navigation satellite, NVS-03, marking a significant step towards strengthening the country’s indigenous satellite navigation capabilities. The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-F18), carrying the satellite, lifted off from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh, last night. It was the 20th flight of the GSLV. The satellite was successfully separated from the launch vehicle and placed in its intended Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit. NVS-03 is the third satellite in ISRO’s second-generation navigation satellite series. It is designed to ensure continuity and improve the availability of navigation services under the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), India’s indigenous regional navigation system. The satellite carries an indigenous atomic clock along with procured atomic clocks. It also introduces the L1 frequency band, in addition to the existing L5 and S bands, enhancing the capabilities of the navigation system. These advancements are expected to strengthen India’s independent positioning, navigation and timing capabilities for civilian, strategic and security applications. Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan has congratulated the entire ISRO team on the successful launch of the GSLV-F18 mission. In a social media post, he said the achievement would further strengthen NavIC and enhance the country’s satellite-based navigation capabilities. He added that the successful mission reflected India’s growing capabilities in space technology and its commitment to self-reliance in advanced technologies. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also congratulated the scientists, engineers and the entire ISRO team on the successful launch. In a social media post, he said the mission marked an important step towards strengthening NavIC, India’s indigenous satellite navigation system. He added that NVS-03, equipped with enhanced capabilities, would further strengthen the country’s navigation infrastructure and contribute to India’s vision of self-reliance in critical and advanced technologies. ISRO Chairman Dr V. Narayanan congratulated the scientists, engineers, industrial partners and academic institutions associated with the mission. Addressing the gathering after the launch, he said the satellite, weighing approximately 2,232 kilograms, had been precisely injected into its intended transfer orbit. He also highlighted that the mission was accomplished with a turnaround time of just 56 days between two successive GSLV missions, the shortest interval achieved so far. Speaking to the media, Dr Narayanan said ISRO had placed its third indigenous atomic clock in orbit aboard NVS-03, while two indigenous atomic clocks were already functioning in orbit. He added that the satellite had been launched as part of India’s Regional Navigation Satellite System, which aims to provide navigation services across the country and up to 1,500 kilometres beyond its borders. Explaining the programme, the ISRO Chairman said it envisages a constellation of seven satellites in orbit to provide these services. He added that NVS-03 was the fourth satellite launched under the programme and that signals from four satellites could be used for multiple purposes. He said the constellation would need to be completed before navigation services could be integrated with mobile systems for wider public use.

national_raw_news.content: The nation is paying homage to the great freedom fighter Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his 151st birth anniversary today. The day is observed as Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, or National Unity Day. President Droupadi Murmu and Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan paid floral tributes to Sardar Patel at his statue at Patel Chowk in New Delhi. Prime Minister Narendra Modi also paid tributes to the Iron Man of India, saying that Sardar Patel dedicated his life to building a strong, prosperous and capable India. Union Home Minister Amit Shah, Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj also paid floral tributes to the great national leader. Later, Union Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off the Run for Unity at the Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium to mark Rashtriya Ekta Diwas. Speaking on the occasion, Mr Shah said Sardar Patel was a great personality who not only transformed the nation’s history but also shaped its geography. He added that India stands proudly on the global stage today because of the strong foundations laid by Sardar Patel. Popularly known as the Iron Man of India, Sardar Patel served as the country’s first Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister. He played a historic role in integrating more than 560 princely states to build a united and strong India. Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrates his immense contribution to the political integration and unity of the country. The occasion also serves as a reminder of the importance of national unity, integrity, security and harmony in India’s diverse and vibrant society. Government institutions, schools and colleges are organising unity pledges, cultural programmes and awareness activities across the country to commemorate Sardar Patel’s ideals and legacy. The Run for Unity is also being organised at various places to spread the message of national integration, peace and brotherhood.
